name: Ezekiel 25:17
description_md:
__Ezekiel 25:17__ I'm a huge fan of borrowing from different intellectual properties when a specific actor plays a role in both of them, and of course here the actor is Samuel L. Jackson who played our boy Nick Fury in the MCU and the gangster Jules Winnfield in Pulp Fiction! After playing Nick Fury a few times I realized I wanted to play him like I play Vision and stay in Stealth mode for most of the game and blast away with damage which doesn't come from an _Attack_! See it in action __here__ against Black Widow! Nick will strike down upon foes ___"with great vengeance and Fury-ous anger"___ using several cards which deal damage but don't force a flip to Assault * [Bombs Away](/card/42029) * [Audacity](/card/21046) * [Sky-Destroyer](/card/50057) * [Tac Team](/card/01056) But when you do want to go to Assault for a +3 attack, keep one of the following at hand to flip back to Stealth: * [Concentrated Fire](/card/50037) * [Covert Surveillance](/card/50038)
__Side Schemes__ * [Build Support](/card/40027) is here for [Fury's Flying Car](/card/50040) (it gives you ___AERIAL___ which you need to play [Bombs Away](/card/42029)) - but if you already have it in play, use it for [Sky-Destroyer](/card/50057) * [Keep Up the Pressure](/card/46018) is here for [Concentrated Fire](/card/50037) or [Spray Fire](/card/50039) * [Superpower Training](/card/40059) is here for [Fury's Watch](/card/50044) - but if you already have that in play use it for [Eyepatch Camera](/card/50043) or [EM Shield](/card/50042)
__Pulp Fiction, 1994__ The path of the righteous man is beset on all sides by the
Inequities of the selfish and the tyranny of evil men
Blessed is he who, in the name of charity and good will
shepherds the weak through the valley of darkness
for he is truly his brother's keeper and the finder of lost children
And I will strike down upon thee with great vengeance and furious
Anger those who attempt to poison and destroy my brothers
And you will know
My name is the Lord when I lay my vengeance upon thee
__Yes of course that's a real bible quote, but Quentin Tarantino rewrote it to sound more cinematic (I guess lol) for Pulp Fiction :)__
